text: String changed its internal storage in Java 9 and no source code anywhere needed altering. What made that possible?
choices: Users only ever used the interface, never the representation
The change was backward compatible at the byte level
explanation: length(), charAt(), substring() — that is all anyone used, so switching from char[] to a byte array with an encoding flag affected essentially every Java program and required nothing from anybody. That is what the separation buys, at a scale worth taking seriously.
